scope.also_moved_note: Neither is a free choice. The profile is the fixture's own declared choice for these five files, and the adapter stage does not exist for a producer that writes the neutral plan itself. Both are consequences of the source shape and are recorded as such, not as second variables.
scope.measured_against_note: Run-21 is the harness this cell is translated from and the cell whose protocol it repeats. Its figures are the document cell's and none of them is an expectation of this one: a document with 186 blocks and five source files with eight rows between them cannot be compared by record count, row count or token count. What carries across is the outcome and the number of structural returns.

required_pieces_moved.why: DERIVATION_CONTENT_CHECKS names the document adapter's checks (NOT_VERBATIM, DIGEST_MISMATCH, MODALITY_NOT_ASSERTED and their kin). None of them runs on a plan the producer wrote, so requiring it here would be pinning a mechanism this cell never reaches. The plan compiler's checks are what bind, and the shipped structural bundle is the admission path the runner takes, so both are pinned instead.

PLAN_DERIVATION_CHECKS.document_adapter_note: the document adapter's derivation content checks are DIGEST_MISMATCH, NOT_VERBATIM and their kin; they bind a document capture and not a plan the producer wrote, so this cell does not carry them as a verified piece

history.chosen_by_evidence: research/ontology_driven_kg_realization/experiments/small_shop/public_population/run.py obtains it as malleus.compiler.STATE_VERSION_PROFILE and admits all five plans under it; the paper declares the same bytes.
history.admitted_families_note: The state-version profile's Event ontology role is empty, so no event or event-participation record can be admitted under it. A producer that writes one is refused FAMILY_NOT_ADMITTED.

producer.harness: Claude Code Agent tool, subagent_type general-purpose, no inherited context
producer.reasoning_effort: harness default, not pinned or observed
producer.boundary: declared session boundary over a shared workspace, not an operating-system sandbox
producer.inputs_note: Run-21's six input kinds with two replaced: the five Small Shop source files stand where the selected reading stood, and the shipped state-version profile stands where the source-assertion profile stood. The state-version profile is the Small Shop fixture's own declared choice, read from public_population/run.py, and not a paper selection.
producer.forbidden_inputs_note: The nine are run-21's, unchanged. What each excludes here: PRIOR_ONTOLOGY covers the Small Shop base contract and every fixture t-box; PRIOR_POPULATION covers public_population/plans/ and the pareto, correction and settlement mappings; PRIOR_RESULT covers public_population/evidence.json and every fixture evidence file; REPOSITORY_DOCUMENTATION covers public_population/README.md. The producer writes its own ontology from the rows, as the document producer writes its own from the reading.

population.plan_order_note: The runner admits the plans in file-name order, so a supersession must sit in a file that sorts after the state it supersedes. The spawn message tells the producer to name the files that way.

contract_identity.why: A document producer never writes a contract identity: the adapter writes it from the retained history. A producer that writes its own neutral plans has to carry it and cannot compute it, because the identity binds the validated fact set to the shipped structural admission profile, which is not a declared input. The parent computes it between the gate and phase two and supplies it with the plan coordinate.

population.census_not_reported: There is no census for rows. The census is the document adapter's report and adapt_document_assertions is the only thing in Core that produces one; compile_population_plan produces none. Every field run-21's census carries is a fact about a document capture and has no reading for a plan: blocks_total, blocks_asserted, blocks_declared_nothing_assertable and blocks_untouched, because there are no blocks; assertions and assertions_by_formalization, because there are no assertions; the subject axis (proposed, attachable, ambiguous, unnamed), because a subject is a reference the reading names in a formalizing sentence; and provenance_coverage's assertion_locator and statement_sha256 halves, because a row-derived record binds no statement bytes. What survives as a count is read from the run result and the trace summary instead: records by family, derivations per record, gaps by kind, and sources per plan.
population.runner_deviation_from_the_fixture: The fixture assembles its own protocol machine, policy and history binding from experiments/small_shop/pareto/ and admits with hand-written machine events. The runner uses the shipped structural bundle through create_structural_history and admit_structural_change instead. That is the same admission path run-21's runner takes, and it is why no Core protocol internal is named in any file of this cell.

query.binding_preflight_why: E-0196 and E-0198. Run-21's first binding named a parent type without a surface subtype, the facade's typed query returned the subtype's records, and the executor refused after admission. The check runs at acceptance, where the evaluator can still correct the set and no row exists.

CQ-S2.reason: The superseded state is not in the current graph. The executor's ENTITY case returns admitted records of a type through the facade's typed query, which projects the current non-superseded records the state-version profile selects, so the earlier state cannot be a row.
CQ-S2.judged_from: results/trace-summary.json, whose per-record supersedes_record_id, superseded_by and valid_to carry the history half
CQ-S2.executor_not_extended: The executor stays type-only. Adding a history reach would make the binding something other than the binding every closed cell ran.

CQ-S4.reason: A derivation locator and a source id live in the retained plan and the trace, not in the graph. A type-only case names record types and projected field names and cannot filter by source.
CQ-S4.judged_from: results/trace-summary.json and the query trace summary, whose per-record derivations carry the source id and the row locator for every field
CQ-S4.executor_not_extended: Same reason. The reviewer reads the trace; the executor does not gain a provenance predicate.

duties_moved.why: A row-derived record binds no statement bytes. There is no assertion_locator and no statement_sha256, so the digest token has nothing to recompute. What replaces it is the one check the reviewer can make that Core does not: open the row the locator names and compare the value.

review_input_manifest.materials: the five source files, the questions, the binding, the query result, the population trace summary, the query trace summary, and the retained plans in place of the retained capture

review_protocol.detail: The frozen v2 validator refuses any protocol whose evidence_surface.authoritative is not SELECTED_READING_TEXT_LAYER and whose locator_kind is not SELECTED_READING_BLOCK_ID, and it requires fixed_identities to carry exactly source_sha256, selected_reading_sha256 and competency_questions_sha256. It also requires a review record's question ids to equal the protocol's, which are CQ-01 to CQ-04. This cell's evidence surface is five row-shaped files, its locators are rows and fields, and its questions are CQ-S1 to CQ-S4. No shop protocol was written, because any file this cell could write would be refused by the frozen validator, and the validator is frozen for a reason.
review_protocol.decision_for_luis: Either the evaluation layer gains a v3 protocol and validator that admit a non-document evidence surface, or shop-01's questions are renamed CQ-01 to CQ-04 and the v2 protocol's fixed identities are re-read for this cell. The first is a change to a frozen validator; the second makes two cells' CQ-01 mean different questions. Neither was taken here.
review_protocol.consequence: The preliminary review record for this cell cannot be machine validated by paper-v4/evaluation-v4/review.py until that decision is taken. Everything before the review runs and is tested.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/bind_from_surface.py
changes.detail: The evaluator writes one file of type sets per question, read from the accepted population surface at ontology acceptance and before phase two exists. bind_from_surface.py expands it deterministically into the exhaustive binding: every ordered pair of a question's types under every relation type on the surface, with a fixed field projection per type made of that type's non-housekeeping slots, carrying bound_at_stage ONTOLOGY_ACCEPTANCE. Its digest is recorded in the launch log at acceptance and the query runs it unchanged after replay; only bound_after_replay_receipt_sha256 moves from PENDING to the receipt digest, and cases_sha256 digests the queries alone so the executed binding is provably the one the launch log pinned. The producer never sees any of it.
changes.why: Deep sweep D-01. Run-04's own binding records in bound_by that a hand-picked draft returned no row for CQ-03 and was replaced, and that a second draft's CQ-04 type set was cut once its 75 citation rows were visible. No value or identifier entered the binding, but the selection between bindings was conditioned on the result, which the manuscript's binding rule and the master plan's submission gate both exclude in kind.

This producer must, and it cannot compute one from its declared inputs, so the parent computes it. The alternative, letting the producer see the admission profile, would give it an input no document cell had.

changes.subject: src/malleus/_contract_pipeline/document.py
changes.detail: Four fixes to what the protocol reports, none to what it admits. The block census labels every block of the reading ASSERTED, DECLARED_NOTHING_ASSERTABLE or UNTOUCHED and counts the three, keeping blocks_reviewed as the sum of the first two with its meaning stated. A provenance axis reports, per type that carries assertion_locator, how many records reach the assertion behind them and how many bind its bytes. The rehydration failure that reached run-17's runner as a raw ValueError is typed RECORDS_NOT_REHYDRATABLE in the plan compiler's enum. GAP_REQUIRED runs as a pre-pass that collects every assertion with neither a formalization target nor a gap and refuses once, instead of naming the first.
changes.why: Run-16 and run-17 both left the record saying something that is not true. Run-16's census counted 186 of 186 blocks reviewed when 128 of them were a producer claim the census cannot check; run-17's counted 186 when the capture named seven. The two protocol observations of E-0176 are the other half: the paper claims every refusal is typed, and at the rehydration stage that was false, and GAP_REQUIRED spent a return on one assertion when eight were in the same state. This cell reads the fixes because its producer is the one that met all four.
changes.expected_reasons_basis: One reason is typed where the graph gate's exception passed through untyped, and none is removed. The pin computes the difference of the plan compiler's enum between the v4.9 coordinate and the pinned commit and compares it to this list; the document adapter's enum is expected to be unchanged and the pin records that difference too.
changes.aggregation_non_evidence: The document adapter's enum carries GAP_REQUIRED at both coordinates, so the enum difference cannot report the aggregation. What the AST can see is _empty_assertion_defects, which collects every empty assertion, and _refuse_gaps, which renders them as one refusal, both module-level functions and neither present at the v4.9 coordinate. That is what this entry records and it is recorded as what it is.
changes.pin_evidence: The pin resolves the three block labels inside _block_census by AST and records every label-shaped constant it finds, so a fourth label is reported rather than hidden; it records whether the adapter writes provenance_coverage as a literal; it computes the plan compiler's enum difference between the two coordinates; and it resolves the two GAP_REQUIRED functions by name. LANDED requires all six observations, and the adapter and the plan compiler both moved since the v4.9 coordinate.

A third refusal says the list does not substitute for a producer's own validator even for the producer that writes one; an UNSUPPORTED row says the rows this harness returns stopped being supported by the reading.
changes.not_this_cell: Nothing is claimed about any model, and nothing about the list beyond this document and this producer. One cell is one observation. A cell that is admitted will not have shown that the paragraph caused it, only that the outcome the loop predicted from it occurred.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/native_query.py
changes.detail: native_query.py emits one row per distinct witness per question. A witness is the row's kind and its record ids: record_id for an ENTITY row, record_id and subject_id for a SUBJECT row, relation_id with both endpoint ids for a RELATION row. Two cases that reach one witness produce one row; the row carries case_ordinals, every producing ordinal sorted, in place of case_ordinal, and the rows of a question are ordered by the first ordinal that produced them. The row projects the fields of the witness record's own type as the surface declares them and never the type its case named: for a SUBJECT row each side through its own record's type, for a RELATION row the relation's own type and each endpoint's own type. The per-type projections are read back out of the binding, where the binder already wrote one list per record type off the accepted surface and repeated it in every case naming that type, so bind_from_surface.py does not change and the binding frozen at acceptance with its cases_sha256 stays the executed binding's proof. A type the binding projects two ways, and a record whose own type the binding never names, are both refused rather than guessed past. The subject side still projects tags (E-0156). The result schema moves to malleus.paper-v4.query-result/v3. Nothing else in the executor moves: the three case kinds, the source-free guard, the forbidden-attempt counters and the witness tracer are the bytes every cell from run-02 onward ran, and the producer never sees the file. A second row for a witness the question has already returned is not a second piece of evidence, and a row that shows an ancestor's fields shows the reviewer less than the capture holds.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/run.py
changes.detail: Run-21's runner with the adapter stage removed and a plan loop in its place. It compiles the ontology closure, creates the structural history, retains the five sources verbatim through the shipped retain subcommand, then per plan compiles it, names its retention events through population_retention_events, prepares and admits it, and finally discards every handle, reopens, replays, and compares the reopened receipt and export against the admitted ones. Every call is public malleus.compiler or its shipped CLI.
changes.why: adapt_document_assertions has no input here: there is no capture. The admission path itself is unchanged, which is the point of the cell: if the plans are admissible, they are admissible through the same governed path the document cells use.

No stage number is entered by hand.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/native_query.py, paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/bind_from_surface.py
changes.detail: The native query binding moves to v3 with three case kinds, all type-only and value-blind. RELATION is run-08's shape: a source type, a relation type, a target type and a projection each. ENTITY names one record type and its projected fields and no relation, so every admitted record of that type is a row whose witness is itself. SUBJECT names a source-asserted record type and a subject entity type, and every record of the first whose subject resolves to a record of the second is a row projecting both. native_query.py executes all three, keeps the source-free guard and the forbidden-attempt counters unchanged, and traces every witness through trace_population_record. bind_from_surface.py expands the evaluator's type sets into all three: RELATION as now, ENTITY for every type in the question's set, and SUBJECT for every ordered pair of a subject-bearing type in the set with an entity type in the set. cases_sha256 still digests the queries alone and the binding stays frozen at ontology acceptance exactly as run-08's, with only bound_after_replay_receipt_sha256 moving after the replay. Carried into v4.4: the three kinds, the executor and the freeze stage are this cell's too. One line of the ENTITY expansion is restricted, under ENTITY_KIND_RESTRICTED, and the binding schema moves to v4 with it.
changes.why: handover/2026-09-05-v42-rca.md, follow-up 2, approved in E-0139, and E-0138. Run-08's binding returned 5, 2, 0 and 1 rows over four questions from 2,084 cases because the surface it could reach was relations only, while the answers existed as unattached records: 34 depth quantities and 20 CO2 quantities among 131 observations. An entity-level case kind would have returned every one of them for CQ-03.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/producer-input-manifest.json
changes.detail: The producer reads five structured source files instead of one selected reading, under the same installed skill at the same Core commit, with the same producer block. The skill's own instruction for this case is one sentence: for structured sources, write a source-specific adapter that emits the same neutral population plan. Phase one is unchanged: the producer writes an ontology and the gate compiles it against the declared closure. Phase two changes shape: the producer writes the neutral population plans itself, where the document producer writes a capture that Core's adapter turns into one.
changes.why: Luis, 2026-09-06: what the document cells did not show is whether a model given rows and the same skill would produce an admissible population. Every closed cell of the loop reads prose. The Small Shop plans that prove the structured path are adopter-authored and were written by hand, so nothing in the record says a model can write them.
changes.producer_visible_note: The producer sees the five source files, the profile and the spawn message. It does not see this contract, the questions or the binding.

changes.sentence: Reading the next row is not invention; stop only when every row of every source is populated or carried as a typed gap, or when the next addition would require invention.
changes.detail: One sentence after "Stop when another addition would require invention." Nothing else in the message changes: it is run-04's message with the run id substituted. The added sentence names REVIEWED and nothing_assertable, both of which the installed skill and the capture grammar already carry, and it carries no modelling instruction and no question-derived string.
changes.why: Deep sweep D-22. Run-05 reviewed 27 of 186 blocks against run-02's and run-04's 186, on a stop rule the skill's own step 6 contradicts in terms. A five-fold coverage difference between cells whose only declared variable was the model is a confound, and the sentence is what removes it.
changes.moved: The clause names rows where run-21's names blocks and nothing_assertable, because a source file has rows and no block inventory. The rule it states is the same rule and it is the only sentence of the message that carries a source-shape word.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/shop-01/native_query.py
changes.detail: native_query.py projects the subject entity's tags beside whatever the binder named for the subject side of a SUBJECT row, wherever the subject record carries the slot. _project already drops a field the record does not have, so a subject with no tags projects exactly what it projected in run-12. The edit is in the executor and not in the binder, because the binder's projection is per record type and its housekeeping set is what the RELATION and ENTITY kinds are projected through too: adding tags there would move every row of every kind and the case bytes with them. Nothing else moves. The case field set is closed at the same keys, output_fields is unchanged, cases_sha256 still digests the queries alone, the binding schema stays malleus.paper-v4.native-query-binding/v4, and the record side of a SUBJECT row, the RELATION rows and the ENTITY rows are byte for byte what run-12's executor returned. The producer never sees the file. run-13's test_pipeline.py states the delta as three exact substitutions and reverses them back to run-12's bytes, so a fourth edit fails the test rather than travelling unnoticed. Carried into v4.9 with the executor it lives in. The subject side still projects tags wherever the subject record carries them; what it projects them beside is now the fields the subject record's own type declares rather than the fields the case named, which is ONE_ROW_PER_WITNESS_OWN_TYPE_PROJECTION's doing and not this entry's. A subject with no tags still projects exactly what it projected before. Carried into run-16 inside an executor that is run-15's byte for byte. Carried into run-17 inside an executor that is run-16's byte for byte. Carried into run-18 inside an executor that is run-17's byte for byte. Carried into run-19 inside an executor that is run-18's byte for byte. Carried into run-20 inside an executor that is run-19's byte for byte. Carried into run-21 inside an executor that is run-20's byte for byte.
changes.why: Run-11's preliminary review, carried in the overseer journal as the first item of the harness queue after run-12. Nine SUBJECT rows were tokened SUBJECT_NOT_IN_BLOCK because the row showed the entity's name, the full form, where the block wrote the abbreviation one of the entity's tags carries. The check at capture is Core-15's and accepts either form, so the adapter had already agreed the name is in the block; the row was showing the reviewer less than the check had read. Projecting tags beside the name puts the reviewer and the adapter on the same evidence. It is a review-surface change and not a measurement change: no row is added, removed or reordered. The v4.6 RCA states the effect expected of it: the subject-in-block token no longer flagging an abbreviation the entity's tag already carries.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/type_set_closure.py
changes.detail: The evaluator runs the closure check on its type sets, against the accepted surface and the validated contract, before bind_from_surface.py writes the acceptance binding. A set that names a type without one of its surface subtypes is refused there.
changes.why: E-0196 and E-0198. Run-21's binding was frozen at acceptance, and the executor refused it after admission because an AnalyticalMethod record came back under Method with no projection. The module is the experiment root's and is called from there; this cell copies no part of it.
